sources.finding: CAF ideally recommends three to four levels, while separately documenting the six-level service bound excluding tenant root/subscriptions. The ALZ intermediate root is below tenant root. Sandbox purpose, platform placement, workload requirements and dedicated connectivity need explicit organizational designation; no naming/count predicate. Dedicated regional connectivity subscriptions can be justified by scale.

sources.finding: Single-parent hierarchy supports six MG levels below tenant root, excluding subscriptions. This is a service maximum, not CAF's ideal or a universal four-level counting convention. Partial positive parentage and selected scope cannot designate tenant root, establish complete estate depth, subscription absence, policy results or effective permissions.

sources.finding: defaultManagementGroup governs new subscription placement, not existing membership or absence of root subscriptions. requireAuthorizationForGroupCreation requires root write permission for creation, not all effective privileged operations. Settings read/write permissions themselves grant no other hierarchy/resource access.
